sections.html:
A direct cash sale is the quickest way to sell a Shaler house, because it skips the lender and appraisal steps that stretch out a listing. Shaler Township, in Allegheny County, also has its own pre-closing checklist that every seller has to clear, and that checklist drives the schedule whichever route you choose.

The township's Selling Your Home guide spells out what the seller does, what the closing company orders, and what the buyer sets up afterward. Knowing it in advance keeps a fast sale from stalling in the last week.

Housing here is stable and mostly owner-occupied: 87.0% of units are owned, the median owner-occupied value is $245,500, and median household income is $95,654 across 12,314 households. Median rent is $1,226 a month. With 95.8% of residents in the same house a year earlier, many sellers are long-time owners who are downsizing or settling an estate, and a cash buyer who takes the house as it stands suits them well.

Shaler requires a dye test, a backflow preventer check and a final water reading from the seller, plus four township letters the closing company orders. Every document on the list is required for closing.

  • Dye test. The home is tested to confirm that downspouts and rain leaders are not tied into the sanitary sewer. Results stay valid for three years. Request the test at least 14 days before closing.
  • Backflow preventer. At least two weeks before closing, call the Hampton Shaler Water Authority at (412) 486-4867 for a visit to confirm a dual check valve and thermal expansion tank are in place.
  • Final meter reading. Sellers and landlords schedule a final reading and send a copy to the closing company so escrowed funds can be released.
  • Trash account. Close the account with the hauler and leave the recycling cart for the new owner.

If the dye test fails, the plumber notifies the township and the owner. Repairs can go to any contractor, but the township's building inspector must hear about it at least 24 hours before work starts so the work can be inspected.

The dye test itself is paid separately. Three plumbers under contract with the township charge $30, $35 and $40 per test, and you may hire your own registered plumber if the dye test form and waiver go back to the township office.

For a sale or refinance, give the closing company three years of township and school district real estate tax receipts. The closing company may use those receipts or order a tax certification letter from the township for $50.

Property tax in Shaler involves the county, the township and the school district, so a bill can come from more than one place. If you have lost old receipts, call the township tax office at 412-486-9700 and ask for copies before the closing company needs them.

Pennsylvania's realty transfer tax is 1 percent of the property's value, and local governments add their own share. The Allegheny County Recorder of Deeds collects all of it when the deed is recorded. Buyer and seller are both legally liable, though the sales agreement normally says who pays.

Some transfers are exempt, including certain moves between family members and property passed by will or intestate succession. If the house is part of an estate, ask the Recorder or the closing company which exemption, if any, fits your deed. Ask the Recorder for the current local rate for Shaler before you work out your net proceeds.

Both can affect a Shaler house, depending on the street. The township keeps FEMA flood maps on file and zone maps for Girtys Run, Little Pine Creek and Pine Creek, which flood periodically. The building and zoning office at 300 Wetzel Road will review the maps with you and help work out which flood zone a property is in.

Part of the township sits over land that was mined in the past. The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection sells mine subsidence insurance because homeowner policies usually leave it out. Coverage of $150,000 costs $41.25 a year, and a buyer needs a new policy of their own because the seller's does not carry over. Sellers who cancel at closing can get unused premium back if they notify DEP within 30 days of the sale.

sections.h2: What the buyer handles after closing
sections.html:
Shaler buyers register for the 1 percent earned income tax with Keystone Collections Group and open a water and sewer account with the Hampton Shaler Water Authority, since both charges share one bill. They also set up trash service, which is mandatory under the township code and handled by the township's contracted hauler.

If the property will sit empty for longer than three weeks, the owner can apply for a trash waiver good for up to six months and renewable. A seller who knows the house will be vacant before closing should ask about it.

sections.h2: Is a cash offer a good fit?
sections.html:
It is worth pricing when the house needs work, the dye test or backflow check looks like a problem, or the family wants a closing date it can plan around. A cash buyer is usually willing to take on the township checklist, but ask who pays for the dye test, the $50 letters and any repairs before you sign.

Compare the offer against a listing net of commission and the transfer tax. If the gap is small, the speed may be worth it. If it is large and the house is in good shape, a traditional listing may still make sense.

sections.h2: A two-week plan for a Shaler sale
sections.html:
1. Order the dye test right away, and ask the township or one of its contract plumbers for a time slot.
  2. Call the Hampton Shaler Water Authority for the backflow check, and ask for the water lien letter at the same time.
  3. Gather three years of tax receipts, or call the township tax office for copies.
  4. Tell the closing company to order the No Lien Letter, the Zoning Compliance Letter and the Dye Test Certificate.
  5. Schedule the final meter reading and close the trash account.

If you are selling a vacant or inherited house, shut off service through the water authority and ask about the trash waiver while the property sits empty. The township's requirements apply to every sale, so the same checklist covers an as-is cash purchase.

faqs.q: Does Shaler Township require an occupancy permit to sell a house?
faqs.a: No. Occupancy permits are not required for the sale or refinance of a property. A dye test, backflow check and several township letters are required instead.

faqs.q: How long is a Shaler dye test valid?
faqs.a: Three years from the test date, and the township keeps the result on file. Request the test at least 14 days before closing so a failed result can be fixed in time.

faqs.q: Who orders the Shaler no lien letter?
faqs.a: The closing company orders it from the township for $50. It confirms that no municipal liens are unfiled against the property, and the water authority issues its own separate lien letter.

faqs.q: How much is Shaler's tax certification letter?
faqs.a: The township charges $50 for it. The closing company can use three years of tax receipts instead, so keep those handy, and call the township tax office at 412-486-9700 for copies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant or inherited house in Shaler as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the township's closing requirements are met, because they apply to every sale. Notify the water authority if the house is empty so service can be shut off, and ask about the trash waiver while it sits.
